long_biography.plain_text:
Former Google chief executive Eric Schmidt has channelled technology wealth into open, collaborative research through Schmidt Sciences and Schmidt Ocean Institute. The former backs work across artificial intelligence, astrophysics, biosciences and climate; the latter gives scientists access to oceanographic expeditions and shares the resulting knowledge. He established both initiatives with Wendy Schmidt, extending a philanthropic programme they began in the 2000s.

Schmidt remains an active builder as chief executive and executive chairman of Relativity Space, while serving as a founding partner of venture firm Innovation Endeavors. His wider public work has concentrated on the strategic consequences of emerging technologies: he chaired the US National Security Commission on Artificial Intelligence and founded the Special Competitive Studies Project. His books likewise translate experience in computing and corporate leadership into arguments about how artificial intelligence may reshape society.
